title: Mapsha’ah

paragraphs: [Nedarim 10b](https://www.sefaria.org/Nedarim.10b.7) reads, “Mapsha’ah taught.” [Rashi](https://www.sefaria.org/Rashi_on_Nedarim.10b.7.2) and [the Rosh](https://www.sefaria.org/Commentary_of_the_Rosh_on_Nedarim.10b.2-3) explain that this is a sage’s name. Hyman reports that the Rosh’s commentary reads “Rav Yosef Mapsha’ah taught.” He calls this a scribal error and says the words came from the preceding line, “Rav Yosef taught.”[^2]

notes.text: The longer Rosh reading adds Rav Yosef before Mapsha’ah. No geographical “of Mapsha’ah” is present in the supplied Hebrew. The explanation that the words came from the preceding line is Hyman’s.

The linked Rosh calls Mapsha’ah a sage and mentions Rav Yosef in the preceding separate comment. Hyman quotes the longer reading “Rav Yosef Mapsha’ah taught” and explains it as a copy from that preceding line.
